definition: Whenever the rule fires under its hypotheses, its conclusion is correct.
boundary: Does not imply the rule is implemented or reachable.

definition: A typed operation exists in the runtime/carrier.
boundary: Does not imply a live guard or path.

definition: A finite admissible path reaches a state in which the operation can fire.
boundary: Does not imply that any actual run takes the path.

definition: A run record shows that the operation fired.
boundary: One occurrence does not imply robustness or necessity.

definition: Occurrence persists across declared perturbations or repetitions.
boundary: Robust recurrence still does not establish universality.
